subject.title: [Bug]: claude-cli backend SIGKILLs entire process tree at turn end — Workflow / background tool orphans have no opt-out

question: Should Claude CLI live-session cleanup remain unconditional at turn end, or should OpenClaw add a bounded drain/telemetry contract for in-flight CLI-owned background grandchildren?
rationale: Source confirms the reported behavior, but changing it affects process-tree cleanup guarantees, orphan prevention, session truth, and possibly new config/default surfaces; automation should not choose that product contract unilaterally.

options.title: Adopt bounded drain plus telemetry
options.body: Detect in-flight CLI-owned background children, defer cleanup only within a bounded ceiling, and surface any forced cleanup to the parent/session.

options.title: Telemetry first
options.body: Keep unconditional cleanup for now, but snapshot/log or otherwise surface killed grandchildren so the silent failure class becomes observable before changing lifecycle behavior.

options.title: Document unsupported native background work
options.body: Keep cleanup as the contract and route users to OpenClaw exec/process or detached task surfaces for background work that must survive a turn boundary.

recommendation.title: Adopt bounded drain plus telemetry
recommendation.body: Detect in-flight CLI-owned background children, defer cleanup only within a bounded ceiling, and surface any forced cleanup to the parent/session.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice centers on the warm Claude CLI live-session behavior introduced by obviyus and likely needs that area owner's lifecycle direction.
